title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', the long sequel to La Longue Marche. In it he studies, for two elements ρ, σ of a rank-2 type group (G is presumably GL_2 or a close variant), an auxiliary group scheme M_{ρ,σ}. Tori attached to the two elements appear: T_0, T_ρ, T_σ, the latter being presumably the unit tori of the algebras generated by ρ and σ. A normaliser-type group N'_σ also appears, and σ satisfies the Cayley–Hamilton equation σ^2 − v = 0. The previous page builds:
- a homomorphism Θ : M_{ρ,σ} → G;
- an identity component M°_{ρ,σ};
- the subgroup SR°_{ρ,σ} = Ker(Θ|M°) ≅ ST_ρ × ST_σ, the norm-one subtori. This subgroup is central in M°_{ρ,σ}.

This page states the structure theorem.
1. SR° is normal but not central in all of M_{ρ,σ}.
2. Put M^♮ = M/SR° (63) and M^{♮°} = M°/SR°.
3. Θ° induces an isomorphism M^{♮°} ≅ G. Since M/M° ≅ μ_2 × μ_2 via the sign characters (ε, ε_2), this gives an extension 1 → G → M^♮ → μ_2×μ_2 → 1 (64).
4. Θ is trivial on SR° (indeed SR° ⊂ Ker Θ ≅ S'T_ρ × SN'_σ). Hence Θ factors as Θ^♮ : M^♮ → G (65).
5. The restriction of Θ^♮ to the normal subgroup G is the identity. So Θ^♮ is a retraction, and M^♮ ≅ G × Ker Θ^♮ ≅ G × μ_2 × μ_2 (66). This is the standard fact that an extension admitting a homomorphic retraction onto its normal subgroup is a direct product.
6. One gets the extension 1 → ST_ρ×ST_σ → M_{ρ,σ} → G×μ_2×μ_2 → 1 (67), with quotient map (Θ, ε, ε_2).
7. Action of the quotient on the abelian kernel:
   - The preimage of G is M°, in which SR° is central, so G acts trivially.
   - The next page shows that μ_2×μ_2 acts only through the second factor ε_2 = ε_σ(b). That factor fixes ST_ρ and acts on ST_σ via σ ↦ εσ, an involution compatible with σ^2 = v.

Purpose: to describe M_{ρ,σ} as an extension of a split, explicitly known group by a torus with explicit action. The next step defines R°_{ρ,σ}, the preimage of G_m ⊂ G (70). This is presumably a step toward a concrete 'realisation' of M_{ρ,σ} (the forward reference to (102)) in the study of solutions of the loop equation.
errors: The last lines say 'SR_{ρ,σ} est central dans M_{ρ,σ}'. This contradicts the first line of the page ('distingué mais pas central dans M_{ρ,σ}'). The argument needs centrality in M°_{ρ,σ}, which is what was established on the previous page (62). It is a slip of M for M°.
Inconsistent labelling of the sign characters: (61) and the next page use (ε_3, ε_2), while (67) writes (Θ, ε_1/ε_3, ε_2); the digit is overwritten in the manuscript. This is notational only.
In (65), 'trivial sur R_{ρ,σ}' should read SR°_{ρ,σ} (or Ker Θ). Θ need not be trivial on the larger R°_{ρ,σ}, which maps onto G_m by (69)–(70).

ideas.what: Splitting an extension 1→G→E→μ2×μ2→1 as a direct product using a homomorphic retraction E→G
ideas.modern_name: Split extension / retraction onto a normal subgroup gives a direct product

ideas.what: Description of M_{ρ,σ} as an extension of G×μ2×μ2 by the torus ST_ρ×ST_σ, with action factoring through a sign character and acting by σ↦εσ on ST_σ
ideas.modern_name: Structure of a (disconnected) algebraic group as an extension by a central-in-identity-component torus; component-group action
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard algebraic group theory; the specific group M_{ρ,σ} belongs to Grothendieck's unpublished loop-equation notes

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine structural computation (quotient by a central torus, splitting via a retraction, component-group action) inside an unpublished but technical development. Nothing here would surprise a specialist beyond the fact that the whole loop-equation programme remains unpublished.
transcription_corrections: The margin note at the top right reads roughly '(but entier)'; it is possibly 'tout entier', i.e. 'pas central dans M_{ρ,σ} tout entier'.
The labels above the arrow in (67) are written '(Θ, ε_3, ε_2)' with the digit overwritten, not clearly ε_1.
The second-to-last struck line is roughly 'sont-qui-ne-passe'; it is a cancelled fragment, while the replacement 'note, que l'image' is written above.
